hard: Zara and Hadi went on a boat trip off the coast of Sabah on Saturday.
Their uncle, Captain Lee, drove the boat.
Zara wore a green hat and Hadi wore a red cap.
The boat left the harbour at 8 am.
The sea was calm and the sky was bright blue.
The children put on orange life jackets and sat at the front of the boat.
Zara held a small notebook and a pencil.
Soon Hadi shouted and pointed at the water.
A group of 6 grey dolphins was swimming next to the boat.
A white seagull flew above them.
Then 3 of the dolphins began to jump high above the waves.
A dolphin can swim at 30 km each hour, so it is a very fast swimmer.
It breathes air through a hole on top of its head.
Hadi counted the dolphins again and again, and he smiled.
Zara wrote all the facts in her notebook.
Next the boat stopped near a small island.
The children climbed onto the rocks and looked into a deep pool.
The water in the pool was clear and cold.
Hadi could see an orange starfish at the bottom of the pool.
It had 5 arms and it did not move.
A starfish lives on rocks and in rock pools.
A starfish can grow a new arm, but this takes many months.
Hadi wanted to touch the starfish, but Zara said no.
She said the animal could get hurt.
Later Captain Lee pointed at a spout of water far out at sea.
It came from a whale.
A blue whale can grow to 25 m long, so it is the biggest animal on Earth.
A whale eats tiny sea animals called krill.
The whale swam slowly and it did not jump.
Zara could not see the whale, but she saw the spout.
Hadi saw the tail of the whale rise out of the water.
He took a photo of it.
The boat returned to the harbour at 1 pm.
Zara and Hadi thanked Captain Lee and got off the boat.
Captain Lee smiled and said they could come again.
Zara read all the facts to her mother.
It was a great day at sea.

hard: Aina and Danish went to Taman Safari with their class on Sunday.
They rode in a yellow bus and the trip began at 10 am.
Aina wore a white scarf and Danish carried a blue bag.
A ranger called Mrs Rose met the class at the gate.
She gave each child a map of the park.
The children were happy and the day was warm.
The first stop was a wide field of tall gold grass.
A pride of 7 lions lay under a big tree.
A lion can sleep for up to 20 hours each day.
Danish saw a male lion with a thick mane.
He did not wake up, but his tail moved.
Aina took a photo of the pride.
Mrs Rose told the children to stay quiet and calm.
Next the bus drove to a muddy pool.
A tiger sat by the water with 2 cubs.
Every tiger has its own pattern of stripes.
Aina could see orange fur and black stripes.
A tiger can swim, so it likes to cool off in the water.
The mother tiger did not come near the bus, but she watched it closely.
Then the bus passed a forest of tall green trees.
A big gorilla sat in the grass and ate leaves.
Gorillas eat leaves, stems and fruit.
A male gorilla can weigh 200 kg.
A gorilla lives in a family group, so it is never alone.
Danish counted 4 gorillas in the group.
He took a photo of the biggest one.
The last stop was a tall tree full of birds.
A red parrot sat on a branch.
A parrot can copy words from people.
Aina said hello, and the parrot said hello back.
A green parrot sat next to it and did not make a sound.
Danish counted 9 parrots in the tree.
The bus returned to the gate at 3 pm.
Aina and Danish thanked Mrs Rose for the lovely day.
The class waved goodbye to the animals.
It was a great day at the park.

hard: Farid and Nadia went to Green Valley Wildlife Centre on Friday.
Their class arrived at 11 am in a white coach.
There were 12 children in the group.
Nadia wore a red coat and Farid wore a blue cap.
A keeper called Miss Lily met them at the gate.
She led the group past a pond and a small barn.
The first stop was a low wooden pen.
A brown hedgehog lay inside on a bed of straw.
Miss Lily called her Pip.
Pip curled into a tight ball and hid her face.
A hedgehog has about 5000 spines on its back.
The spines help a hedgehog survive danger.
Pip did not bite, and she did not run away.
Next the children walked to a sunny garden.
A large tortoise sat on the warm grass.
Miss Lily called him Gus.
Gus ate a green lettuce leaf very slowly.
A giant tortoise lives for more than 100 years.
Gus did not hide in his shell, and he walked up to the children.
Inside the small barn, a glass box stood on a table.
A grey mouse sat in the box with white seeds.
The mouse chewed a seed and washed its face.
The front teeth of a mouse grow all through its life.
Chewing keeps the teeth short.
The next room was dark and cool.
Miss Lily turned on a purple lamp.
A scorpion glowed under the lamp.
A scorpion uses the sting in its tail to kill insects.
Farid stepped back, but Nadia stayed close to the glass.
Nadia took a photo, but the scorpion did not move.
The last show was outside on the big lawn.
It lasted 40 minutes.
A golden eagle flew over the lawn and landed on a tall pole.
An eagle can see a small animal from far away.
Farid clapped and Nadia cheered.
Later the class waved goodbye to Miss Lily.
Nadia bought a card of Pip and Farid bought a card of Gus.
They sat on the coach and talked about the animals.
It was an exciting day at the centre.
